personality_one_liner: A cockpit-grade operational tool emphasizing glanceability, high contrast, and dense aeronautical metrics.

spacing.rule: Handle spacing correctly dont have extra spaces where its not required, handle padding and margin corectly and subtle for buttons and components

do's: Use solid surfaceSecondary and surfaceTertiary to maintain high-contrast readability.
dont's: Do not use blur or glassmorphism on dense data screens like aviation metrics.

screens.name: Auth
screens.purpose: Login/Signup for pilots to sync their configurations and saved airports.
screens.layout: Full-bleed background image of a night runway approach with a dark gradient scrim (top to bottom). Form inputs placed in the bottom 40% of the screen. High contrast amber CTA button.

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.purpose: Glanceable overview of current location's weather, flight condition, and active alerts.

states.empty: GPS disabled or no location found illustration
states.error: Unable to fetch METAR/TAF data, retry button

screens.layout: Top section: Large text showing airport code and city, immediately paired with a color-coded FAA flight condition badge (VFR/MVFR/IFR/LIFR). Middle: Wind rose visualization with current speed, gust, and direction. Bottom: Horizontal scrollable timeline strip for hourly forecast (24-48h).

screens.name: Search
screens.purpose: Look up airports by ICAO/IATA code or city name.

states.empty: Illustration of cockpit window looking at empty sky, 'Search for an airport'

screens.layout: Sticky search bar at top. List of results with their current FAA flight condition dot (Green/Blue/Red/Magenta) on the right edge of each list item row.

screens.name: Favorites
screens.purpose: Quick access to saved airports and their immediate conditions.

states.empty: Illustration of empty radar, 'No saved airports'

screens.layout: Grid or vertical list of surfaceSecondary cards. Each card acts as a mini-dashboard showing airport code, main wind metric, and the FAA flight condition color as a thin border or left-edge indicator.

screens.name: Settings
screens.purpose: Configure aviation units and app preferences.
screens.layout: List of segmented controls for unit toggles (Knots vs KM/H, Feet vs Meters, °C vs °F). Strict utilitarian layout using surfaceSecondary rows and dividers.

empty_search.alt: Empty sky viewed through airplane cockpit window

instructions_to_main_agent: Implement '7 Dark-First Utility DARK' strictly. The app should look like a cockpit instrument.
Bypass the strict 'no blue/purple' rule ONLY for the FAA flight condition colors. Use the provided vfr, mvfr, ifr, and lifr color tokens for status indicators.
Do NOT use glassmorphism. This app requires high legibility and contrast. Stick to solid surfaceSecondary blocks with subtle borders.
For the Hourly Forecast timeline, build a horizontally scrolling view. Each item should show time, weather icon, and a directional arrow indicating wind direction relative to north.
Implement the wind rose / compass as a custom UI component. It should clearly show N/E/S/W with an indicator for the current wind direction and text for speed/gusts.
Ensure 'Rajdhani' is used for large numbers, metrics, and display titles, and 'IBM Plex Sans' for secondary text and labels.
For the Auth background image, you MUST implement a top-to-bottom gradient scrim using expo-linear-gradient to ensure form inputs and text are readable at the bottom.
Include haptic feedback on tab changes, unit toggles in settings, and search submission.
